parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the moles in each of the four samples.
parts.sample: Sample 1: 2.00 mol. Sample 2: 0.500 mol. Sample 3: 0.499 mol. Sample 4: 0.500 mol.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Identify the sample with the most molecules and justify your answer.

rubric.point: Justification: most moles, so most molecules

parts.sample: Sample 1, the water. It has the most moles, 2.00 mol, and the number of molecules is proportional to moles.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the number of molecules in Sample 3.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain why Samples 2 and 4 have similar amounts in moles but very different masses.

rubric.point: Glucose molecules are about four times heavier

parts.sample: Both hold about 0.500 mol, so the same number of molecules, but each glucose molecule has about 4.1 times the mass of a carbon dioxide molecule.
